column2: What is the key structural difference between Retail Media and Commerce Media?
column3: Retail Media refers specifically to advertising on a retailer's owned properties using its first-party data, whereas Commerce Media is the broader superset extending that commerce data off-site to third-party channels.

column2: What is Agentic Commerce?
column3: Agentic Commerce is an ecosystem where autonomous AI assistants curate product choices, offer personalized recommendations, and execute transactions on behalf of consumers.

column2: How does the rise of agentic shopping assistants threaten traditional retail search ad revenue?
column3: Agentic assistants bypass standard search result pages, eroding the high-intent impression real estate that traditional sponsored search ads rely on.

column2: What is Advertiser Experience (AX) in modern commerce media platforms?
column3: Advertiser Experience (AX) is the end-to-end usability of a buying platform, encompassing self-service workflows, API integration, automated bidding, and transparent measurement.

column2: Concept: Target ROAS Bidding
column3: Definition: An automated bidding algorithm where advertisers set a desired return on ad spend, allowing the system to adjust bids across large catalogs to meet that goal.

column2: Concept: Dynamic Bidding
column3: Definition: A real-time bidding strategy that increases bids when conversion likelihood is high and decreases bids when likelihood is low.

column2: What is a Conversational Search Prompt in agentic retail media?
column3: It is a sponsored native placement embedded within AI recommendation dialogs that guides natural-language user queries toward specific brands.

column2: Term: Sparky (Walmart Connect)
column3: Definition: A consumer-facing AI shopping assistant developed by Walmart that recommends products and hosts conversational search ad placements.

column2: Term: Marty (Walmart Connect)
column3: Definition: A native, advertiser-facing AI tool within Walmart Connect designed to assist marketers with campaign management and execution.

column2: How does Walmart Connect's second-price auction model for Sponsored Products work?
column3: The highest bidder wins the ad placement but only pays slightly above the amount submitted by the second-highest bidder.

column2: What is Incremental Return on Ad Spend (iROAS)?
column3: iROAS is a metric that measures only the additional sales directly caused by advertising, excluding baseline organic purchases that would have occurred anyway.

column2: How does Incremental ROAS (iROAS) typically compare to last-click ROAS in magnitude?
column3: Incremental ROAS is typically 30% to 60% lower than last-click ROAS because last-click attribution credits purchases that organic intent would have driven independently.

column2: What formula defines standard Return on Ad Spend (ROAS)?
column3: $\text{ROAS} = \frac{\text{Total Attributed Sales}}{\text{Total Ad Spend}}$

column2: How is Omnichannel ROAS calculated in retail media networks?
column3: $\text{Omnichannel ROAS} = \frac{\text{Online Sales} + \text{In-Store Sales} + \text{Pickup} + \text{Delivery}}{\text{Total Ad Spend}}$

column2: What is Advertising Cost of Sales (ACOS)?
column3: ACOS is the percentage of attributed sales spent on advertising, calculated as $\text{ACOS} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Ad Spend}}{\text{Total Attributed Sales}}\right) \times 100$.

column2: In Walmart's Polaris search algorithm, what factor holds the single largest weighting at 40%?
column3: Item completeness, which measures product attributes and structured data.

column2: What is the organic rank requirement for a SKU to be eligible for Sponsored Products on Walmart Connect?
column3: The product must organically rank within the top 128 search results for the targeted term.

column2: What minimum Listing Quality Score (LQS) is recommended for optimal ad performance on Walmart Connect?
column3: A Listing Quality Score above 80% is recommended.

column2: What placement constraint exists for conquesting competitor terms under Walmart's Brand Term Targeting?
column3: Conquesting ads are restricted to position 3 and below, as the top two search positions are strictly reserved for brand defense.

column2: In Walmart Connect, what pricing auction model is utilized for Onsite Display banners?
column3: Onsite Display utilizes an eCPM first-price auction model, where winning advertisers pay their exact bid per thousand impressions.

column2: How does Walmart Connect leverage its Vizio acquisition for Connected TV (CTV) advertising?
column3: It integrates SmartCast OS into its ad infrastructure to deliver household CTV targeting grounded in verified first-party shopper data.

column2: What is the harvesting process in retail media search management?
column3: It is the workflow of identifying high-converting keywords from automated discovery campaigns and migrating them into manual exact-match campaigns.

column2: Under the 60/30/10 budget framework for new retail media advertisers, how should funds be distributed?
column3: Allocate 60% to automatic campaigns, 30% to manual campaigns, and 10% to Sponsored Brands.

column2: Why is structured product metadata critical for brands in an agentic commerce environment?
column3: Autonomous AI engines query structured catalog metadata to verify pricing, check stock, and surface items in natural-language recommendations.

column2: According to research, how much performance improvement does AI-driven ad optimization deliver over manual approaches?
column3: AI-driven ad optimization provides a 15% to 20% improvement in campaign performance.

column2: What is the primary operational hurdle reported by 60% of ad buyers surveyed by the IAB regarding retail media networks?
column3: Inadequate collaboration and communication with their retail network partners.

column2: Why do dominant retail media players like Amazon and Walmart lack strong incentives to adopt universal IAB standardization?
column3: Their dominant market share allows them to establish proprietary standards without needing to conform to universal guidelines.

column2: What is closed-loop attribution in retail media?
column3: Closed-loop attribution directly links ad exposure data to actual online or in-store purchase transactions using first-party buyer data.

column2: Term: Cost Per Acquisition (CPA)
column3: Definition: An ad pricing model where the advertiser pays only when a specified user action, such as a purchase or signup, is completed.

column2: How does the Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) model reallocate financial risk between advertisers and publishers?
column3: It shifts financial risk from the advertiser to the publisher, as payment depends entirely on user conversion.

column2: What is an Open Real-Time Bidding (RTB) auction?
column3: An automated ad auction where supply-side platforms offer impressions to multiple demand-side platforms simultaneously in milliseconds.

column2: How does Rithum's retail media automation protect brand profit margins during campaigns?
column3: It automatically pauses media spend when item stock falls below thresholds or when raw product margins decline.

column2: Term: Kevel
column3: Definition: An API-first developer platform that allows engineering teams to build custom, bespoke ad servers for retail media networks.

column2: What is the function of Topsort in the ad tech landscape?
column3: It provides an API-first auction platform designed for rapid deployment of cookieless sponsored listings on small-to-medium marketplaces.

column2: How does retail media revenue create a Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) offset flywheel for retailers?
column3: Ad revenue generated from store traffic subsidizes customer acquisition costs, funding growth that attracts further traffic.

column2: What negative consumer and business outcomes result from inventory oversaturation on retail websites?
column3: Excessive ad density degrades shopping experience, lowers click-through rates, and reduces ad unit pricing.

column2: What is the conversion rate performance hierarchy among search keyword tiers in retail media?
column3: Branded keywords yield the highest conversion rates, followed by category terms, with competitor conquesting terms producing the lowest.

column2: How does generative AI alter traditional paid search keyword strategy on retail sites?
column3: It shifts consumer discovery from strict keyword queries to natural-language, intent-driven, cross-category contextual searches.

column2: What product detail page element provides vital data signals for generative AI shopping recommendations beyond product attributes?
column3: Customer product reviews, which contain rich qualitative details about actual user experience.

column2: Term: Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO)
column3: Definition: The automated personalization of ad creative components in real time using third-party tools to match individual shopper context.

column2: What is the function of a Demand-Side Platform (DSP) like Walmart DSP?
column3: It enables advertisers to programmatically purchase offsite display, video, and CTV inventory using first-party retail shopper data.

column2: How does the combination of Sponsored Products and Onsite Display impact consumer purchasing behavior?
column3: Running both formats simultaneously yields a 3x to 4x increase in the number of shoppers who purchase the advertised products.

column2: What proportion of orders driven by Sponsored Brands on Walmart Connect come from new-to-brand buyers?
column3: Nearly 46% of all orders driven by Sponsored Brands come from new-to-brand buyers.

column2: What attribution uplift occurs when offline in-store purchases are incorporated into digital campaign measurement?
column3: Reported ROAS increases by an average of 20% to 42% when including offline attribution.

column2: What is the primary functional difference between broad match and exact match in retail search auctions?
column3: Broad match triggers ads on related queries and misspellings at lower CPCs, while exact match targets explicit search terms at higher conversion rates.

column2: What constitutes the 'Buy Box' placement on a Walmart product detail page?
column3: It is an ad unit positioned directly beneath the 'Add to Cart' button on competitor product detail pages.

column2: What default click-based attribution window is standard on Walmart Connect?
column3: A 14-day click-based attribution window is standard.

column2: Term: Pacvue Agent
column3: Definition: An AI agent that converts business questions into database queries, manages budgets, and auto-generates executive reports across retail networks.

column2: What is Alexa for Shopping (2026)?
column3: An AI agent from Amazon that combines product expertise with personalized shopping history to deliver native sponsored product recommendations.

column2: Why do physical retailers remain central destinations even as third-party AI agents expand offsite?
column3: Retailers maintain exclusive control over foundational commercial functions, including live local inventory, real-time pricing, fulfillment, and returns.

column2: According to Criteo data, what percentage of agentic tool users still rely on traditional retailer search and sites during purchase journeys?
column3: More than 96% of shoppers using agentic assistants continue to rely on traditional retailer sites and search.

column2: Term: Baseline Sales Measured by Deterministic Data
column3: Definition: A reporting standard that evaluates underlying organic sales strictly using verified first-party transactions rather than statistical modeling.

column2: What is Joint Business Planning (JBP) in retail media networks?
column3: A strategic collaboration framework establishing joint investment, operational commitments, and preferred commercial terms between a retailer and a brand.

column2: What is the primary benefit of utilizing first-party transaction data over third-party cookies for ad targeting?
column3: First-party data offers deterministic purchase history that remains privacy-safe and immune to cookie deprecation.

column2: What click-through rate (CTR) benchmark advantage does Walmart Connect hold over Amazon Ads?
column3: Walmart Connect achieves a average CTR of 0.6%–0.8%, which is approximately three times higher than Amazon's 0.2%–0.3%.

column2: What is the average Cost Per Click (CPC) comparison between Walmart Connect and Amazon Ads?
column3: Walmart Connect average CPCs ($0.35–$0.75) are roughly 55% lower than Amazon Ads average CPCs ($0.85–$5.00+).

column2: Term: Self-Service Ad Center
column3: Definition: A software console allowing brand marketers to directly set up, manage, bid on, and report on ad campaigns without managed service reps.

column2: In Walmart Connect's dynamic bidding system, what is the maximum percentage increase applied to a bid when conversion probability is high?
column3: Bids can dynamically increase by up to +100%.

column2: How long is the recommended learning period before evaluating performance changes on a Target ROAS campaign?
column3: A learning period of 2 to 3 weeks is recommended before making significant adjustments.

column2: What minimum daily budget is required to run a Sponsored Products campaign on Walmart Connect?
column3: A minimum daily budget of $100 is required.

column2: What is the minimum bid requirement for Sponsored Brands on Walmart Connect?
column3: The minimum bid requirement for Sponsored Brands is $1.00.

column2: What is the technical requirement for video length in Walmart Connect Sponsored Video ads?
column3: Video length must be between 5 and 30 seconds.

column2: Why are closed captions mandatory for spoken audio in Sponsored Video creatives on Walmart Connect?
column3: They ensure ADA compliance and accommodate auto-muted video playback within search results.

column2: What recommended monthly budget threshold is suggested for Onsite Display campaigns to achieve meaningful data volume?
column3: A recommended minimum budget is $4,500 per month.

column2: How does Walmart DSP track advertising impact outside of Walmart physical and digital storefronts?
column3: It utilizes rest-of-market analysis to measure sales lift across external retail channels.

column2: What role does Osmos (OsmoSphere & ControlHub) play for independent retailers?
column3: It allows independent retailers to construct a fully white-labeled, self-serve retail media network platform in under four weeks.

column2: What structural shift separates trade spend from modern retail media under the 2026 IAB framework?
column3: Trade spend involves off-invoice category allowances, whereas retail media involves measurable, addressable digital advertising.

column2: What is the minimum character length recommended for product titles on Walmart to avoid Polaris search penalties?
column3: Titles should be concise, ideally between 50 and 75 characters.

column2: What keyword metric in Walmart's Keyword Planner evaluates how frequently a product appears in search results for a specific term?
column3: Item Keyword Frequency (or Item-Level Relevance).

column2: In Walmart's Keyword Planner, what action should an advertiser take for a 'Low-High' keyword opportunity?
column3: Prioritize listing content optimization to build relevancy before scaling ad bids.

column2: What average ROAS return is typically generated by Buy Box placements in Walmart Connect Sponsored Products?
column3: Buy Box placements generate an average ROAS of 6.0x.

column2: How does last-touch attribution affect the reported performance of upper-funnel formats like Display and CTV?
column3: It underreports their performance by assigning full conversion credit to the final bottom-funnel click.

column2: Term: AI Content Generator
column3: Definition: An AI-driven creative software tool that transforms basic product photography into stylized lifestyle images for ad units.

column2: What is the function of sponsored prompts in conversational AI shopping interfaces?
column3: They present suggested questions or follow-up topics to shoppers within chat flows, driving discovery upstream.

column2: How do AI agents optimize ad delivery within limited LLM conversational space?
column3: They dynamically evaluate and balance organic context, bid amounts, and shopper relevance across few available response slots.

column2: What is the primary metric evaluated by advertisers seeking true causal incremental impact rather than correlated revenue?
column3: Incremental Sales Lift measured against a deterministic holdout control group.

column2: What structural risk occurs if retail media relies solely on visual site banners during the agentic era?
column3: Banners lose visibility as consumers migrate interaction away from visual web pages to conversational voice or text prompts.

column2: Why is bid adjustment capped in automated second-price auctions?
column3: Capping automated bid increases prevents run-away auction clearing prices and protects advertiser efficiency goals.

column2: Term: Machine-to-Machine Agent Experience (AX)
column3: Definition: The programmatic interface and structured data architecture that allows external AI agents to query and transact on retail platforms.

column2: What is closed-loop attribution in retail media?
column3: The methodology of directly linking ad exposures to actual downstream transactions using a retailer's deterministic first-party purchase data.

column2: How is standard Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) calculated?
column3: $\text{ROAS} = \frac{\text{Attributed Ad Revenue}}{\text{Total Ad Spend}}$

column2: What is the primary operational flaw of relying solely on standard last-click ROAS?
column3: It credits 100% of conversion value to the last ad touched, capturing organic baseline demand that would have purchased anyway without proving causal impact.

column2: What is incremental ROAS (iROAS)?
column3: A performance metric that measures return on ad spend calculated exclusively on incremental revenue directly caused by the ad, excluding baseline organic sales.

column2: By approximately how much does incremental ROAS typically differ from platform-reported last-click ROAS?
column3: Incremental ROAS typically runs $30\%$ to $60\%$ lower than reported last-click ROAS.

column2: What is a Data Clean Room (DCR) in digital advertising?
column3: A secure, privacy-compliant environment that allows two or more parties to match and analyze pseudonymized datasets without exposing raw user-level PII.

column2: Why are Data Clean Rooms critical for retail media offsite advertising?
column3: They enable privacy-safe identity matching between a retailer's first-party shopper data and a brand's CRM data without third-party cookies or direct PII exposure.

column2: What is a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) in commerce media incrementality testing?
column3: An experimental setup where ad exposure is randomly withheld from a control group to observe the unexposed counterfactual and measure true causal sales lift.

column2: Why are RCTs considered the ground truth for training machine-learning attribution models?
column3: They provide unbiased estimates of ad effects by physically observing the no-ad counterfactual, whereas pure observational models carry severe estimation bias.

column2: What are the four methodology families codified in the November 2025 IAB Commerce Media Incrementality Guidelines?
column3:
1. Experiments (RCTs/Holdouts)
2. Model-based counterfactuals (Synthetic controls)
3. Econometric models (MMM)
4. Hybrid proxies

column2: What three core principles govern all valid incrementality methodologies under IAB guidelines?
column3:
1. Credible counterfactuals
2. Control of bias
3. Separation of signal from noise

column2: How is Advertising Cost of Sale (ACOS) calculated?
column3: $\text{ACOS} = \left( \frac{\text{Total Ad Spend}}{\text{Total Ad Revenue}} \right) \times 100\%$

column2: What is the mathematical relationship between ROAS and ACOS?
column3: ACOS is the inverse of ROAS: $\text{ACOS} = \frac{1}{\text{ROAS}}$ (expressed as a percentage).

column2: How does Walmart Connect calculate Omnichannel ROAS?
column3: $\text{Omnichannel ROAS} = \frac{\text{Online Sales} + \text{In-Store Sales} + \text{Pickup} + \text{Delivery}}{\text{Ad Spend}}$

column2: Including in-store attribution typically increases reported retail media ROAS by what percentage?
column3: Including offline/in-store purchase data typically increases reported ROAS by approximately $20\%$ to $42\%$.

column2: What is the IAB Tech Lab PAIR protocol?
column3: Publisher Advertiser Identity Reconciliation (v1.1): A protocol for secure audience matching and activation between brand and publisher datasets without exposing raw PII.

column2: What is the purpose of the IAB Tech Lab ADMaP protocol?
column3: Attribution Data Matching Protocol (v1.0): Standardizes deterministic transaction matching across data clean room environments for conversion attribution.

column2: What is the MRC display viewability standard?
column3: At least $50\%$ of the ad's pixels must be in view for a minimum of one continuous second.

column2: What is the MRC video viewability standard?
column3: At least $50\%$ of the video pixels must be in view for a minimum of two continuous seconds.

column2: According to IAB guidelines, at what point must a retail media ad impression be counted?
column3: Ad impressions must be counted strictly on a begin-to-render basis (when rendering starts on the client device).

column2: What is the difference between GIVT and SIVT?
column3: General Invalid Traffic (GIVT) consists of routine bots and search crawlers; Sophisticated Invalid Traffic (SIVT) includes complex fraudulent activity like hidden ads, malware, and hijacked devices.

column2: What is Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM)?
column3: A top-down statistical modeling technique that evaluates the contribution of marketing channels to overall sales using macro-level aggregate data without individual tracking.

column2: What is Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA)?
column3: A bottom-up measurement approach that distributes fractional conversion credit across multiple ad touchpoints along a consumer's path to purchase.

column2: What is the Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC)?
column3: Amazon's data clean room solution allowing advertisers to run custom SQL queries on pseudonymized Amazon Ads exposure and retail purchase signals.

column2: What clean room product did Instacart launch to compete with AMC and Walmart Luminate?
column3: Instacart Data Hub (introduced at CES 2026).

column2: What is the recommended standard attribution lookback window for retail media click conversions?
column3: A 14-day attribution lookback window.

column2: What defines a New-to-Brand (NTB) customer?
column3: A shopper who makes a purchase from a brand for the first time within a specified lookback window (typically 90 to 365 days).

column2: Why is pure observational ML attribution prone to severe errors without experimental calibration?
column3: Observational models mistake correlation for causation by crediting ads shown to high-intent users who would have purchased anyway (errors up to $488\% - 948\%$).

column2: What is the principle of least privilege in Data Clean Room design?
column3: Restricting user access strictly to the datasets, queries, timeframes, and computation outputs required for a specific task, preventing raw data extraction.

column2: How do person-level DSPs and account-level DSPs fundamentally differ in targeting unit?
column3: Person-level DSPs target individual consumer profiles or devices (cookies, device IDs); account-level DSPs target companies and buying groups (firmographics, IP resolution).

column2: Why is third-party cookie deprecation less disruptive for account-level B2B targeting than person-level B2C targeting?
column3: Account-level targeting resolves company identities via IP and firmographic data outside browser cookie policy, whereas person-level targeting relies on cross-site tracking cookies.

column2: What is total advertising cost of sale (TACOS)?
column3: $\text{TACOS} = \left( \frac{\text{Total Ad Spend}}{\text{Total Overall Sales (Organic + Ad-Attributed)}} \right) \times 100\%$

column2: What is organic cannibalization in retail media?
column3: When paid search or display ads capture sales from consumers who would have bought the product organically at no ad cost.

column2: In DOOH in-store measurement, what does Opportunity To See (OTS) represent?
column3: The count of qualified individuals present in the display exposure zone while an ad is running—serving as the proxy for a viewable in-store ad impression.

column2: In DOOH in-store standards, how does an 'Ad Play' differ from a 'Gross Impression'?
column3: An Ad Play counts screen playouts without verifying human presence; a Gross Impression multiplies screen playouts by the number of individuals present in the zone.

column2: How do Likelihood-To-See (LTS) impressions refine in-store viewability?
column3: They adjust OTS impression counts using sensor or video analytics to estimate the percentage of present shoppers who actually noticed the screen.

column2: What privacy requirement applies to modern 2026 DOOH in-store audience sensors?
column3: Sensors must measure geometry, height, or signal presence without facial recognition, cameras capturing facial images, or logging raw MAC addresses.

column2: What is synthetic control modeling in incrementality testing?
column3: A model-based counterfactual approach that combines unexposed non-target markets or historical baselines to construct a predictive 'no-ad' comparison group.

column2: What is holdout contamination in an advertising experiment?
column3: When members of the designated control (unexposed) group accidentally receive ad exposures through other channels or unmanaged platforms, distorting the test.

column2: According to Ovative Group analysis, how widely can campaign iROAS vary based solely on matching-methodology choice?
column3: Within-campaign iROAS varies by an average of $6.5\times$ (median $2.5\times$) depending on the selected matching methodology within the same network.

column2: What is the eMarketer CTR performance benchmark threshold for native ads in retail media?
column3: A CTR above $0.4\%$ indicates strong native ad performance.

column2: Which Walmart Connect ad placement delivers the highest typical ROAS?
column3: Buy Box placement, averaging $6.0\times$ ROAS.

column2: According to Walmart Connect benchmarks, what percentage of Sponsored Video ad sales come from new-to-brand customers?
column3: $91\%$ of sales generated by Sponsored Videos are from new-to-brand customers.

column2: What is a Private Marketplace (PMP) deal in programmatic advertising?
column3: An invite-only real-time auction where selected advertisers bid on premium publisher inventory using a unique Deal ID.

column2: How does Programmatic Guaranteed buying differ from Preferred Deals?
column3: Programmatic Guaranteed commits fixed pricing and guaranteed impression volume; Preferred Deals fix pricing with no volume commitment.

column2: How is effective Cost Per Mille (eCPM) calculated for a publisher?
column3: $\text{eCPM} = \left( \frac{\text{Total Ad Revenue}}{\text{Total Served Impressions}} \right) \times 1000$

column2: How does Real Cost Per Mille (rCPM) differ from eCPM?
column3: rCPM divides total revenue by total ad *requests* (including unfilled impressions), measuring true total yield, whereas eCPM counts only delivered impressions.

column2: What is the Sell-Through Rate (STR) formula for ad inventory?
column3: $\text{STR} = \left( \frac{\text{Impressions Sold}}{\text{Total Impressions Available}} \right) \times 100\%$

column2: What is a Customer Data Platform (CDP)?
column3: Software that aggregates and unifies first-party customer data from multiple touchpoints into persistent individual profiles for targeting and activation.

column2: Why are Data Management Platforms (DMPs) declining in ad tech?
column3: DMPs historically depended on third-party tracking cookies, which are undergoing structural browser deprecation.

column2: In B2B account-based advertising, what formula estimates monthly impression needs?
column3: $\text{Monthly Impressions} = \text{Target Account Count} \times (2,500 \text{ to } 3,000 \text{ impressions per account})$

column2: What is Universal ID 2.0 (UID2)?
column3: An open-source, cookieless identity framework that creates salted and hashed identity tokens from consented user email addresses.

column2: What is view-through conversion attribution?
column3: Crediting an ad exposure for a conversion when a user sees an ad, does not click it, but later completes a transaction within the lookback window.

column2: What is the main risk for a publisher running Cost Per Click (CPC) campaigns?
column3: The publisher absorbs engagement risk; if ad creative or placement yields a low click-through rate, delivered impressions generate zero revenue.

column2: What is Cost Per Acquisition (CPA)?
column3: $\text{CPA} = \frac{\text{Total Campaign Spend}}{\text{Total Desired Conversions (sales, leads, downloads)}}$

column2: In retail media measurement, what is halo effect (or 'other sales') attribution?
column3: Attributing purchases of non-advertised products under the same brand or product line when a consumer interacts with an ad for a specific product.

column2: What is basket analysis in retail media reporting?
column3: Analyzing co-purchased SKUs and cross-category items included in the consumer's shopping cart alongside the advertised product.

column2: What is rest-of-market analysis in retail media measurement?
column3: Evaluating whether an ad campaign on one retailer network caused incremental sales lift across external, competing retailers.

column2: What is the function of a Consent Management Platform (CMP)?
column3: Software that collects, stores, and passes user privacy consent choices to ad tech systems to ensure regulatory compliance (GDPR/CCPA).

column2: In programmatic ad buying, what four fee components comprise total CPM cost?
column3:
1. Media cost
2. DSP platform/seat fee
3. Data/audience fees
4. Managed service fees

column2: What is the Media Rating Council (MRC) accreditation?
column3: An independent audit stamp certifying that a measurement provider's metrics adhere to industry audience measurement standards.

column2: Why do B2B retail media and DSP CPMs typically run higher than consumer B2C CPMs?
column3: B2B campaigns target highly specialized, narrow decision-maker audiences rather than mass consumer volume.

column2: What is the primary trade-off of using Open Real-Time Bidding (RTB)?
column3: It offers maximum scale and low CPMs, but carries higher brand safety risk and lower placement quality compared to PMPs.

column2: How is Fill Rate calculated for publisher inventory?
column3: $\text{Fill Rate} = \left( \frac{\text{Ad Impressions Delivered}}{\text{Total Ad Requests Made}} \right) \times 100\%$

column2: What is a dynamic floor price in programmatic auctions?
column3: A minimum CPM threshold set by a publisher that automatically adjusts in real time based on user signals, context, and demand to maximize yield.

column2: According to Amazon Ads research (2025), how does Amazon's Causal Calibration Model structure attribution?
column3: It trains ML models on hundreds of thousands of RCT campaigns to calibrate rule-based, last-touch, and observational ML predictions.

column2: What is the primary role of an Ad Server in the programmatic supply chain?
column3: To host creative assets, make delivery decisions, render ads to the client device, and log impressions and clicks.

column2: What is the 'proof ladder' sequence for retail media performance verification?
column3: Attributed Sales $\rightarrow$ Test vs. Control $\rightarrow$ Holdout Lift $\rightarrow$ MMM Reconciliation $\rightarrow$ Finance Sign-off.

column2: What is the 5-minute iROAS metric introduced by Gulp Media Network?
column3: A store-level metric quantifying immediate sales occurring within 5 minutes after an in-store audio ad plays compared to unexposed store dayparts.

column2: Why is 'recycled demand' a critical concept when evaluating retail media ROI?
column3: Recycled demand consists of existing brand loyalists who would have bought organically; crediting their sales to ads inflates ROAS without driving real growth.

column2: What type of auction mechanism does Walmart Connect use for Sponsored Products?
column3: Walmart Connect uses a second-price auction model, where the winning advertiser pays just above the second-highest bid.

column2: What is the primary function of Sponsored Products on Walmart Connect?
column3: They are cost-per-click native ads that promote individual SKUs in prominent locations to drive shoppers to product detail pages.

column2: Where do Search In-Grid Sponsored Product ads appear on Walmart?
column3: They appear in the top 1–4 slots and every 10 items within search results.

column2: What is the strategic objective of Item Carousel placements on Walmart.com?
column3: To drive cross-selling and capture comparison shoppers viewing product detail pages.

column2: Where is the Buy Box placement for Sponsored Products located, and what is its average ROAS?
column3: It is located directly below the "Add to Cart" button on competitor pages and generates an average ROAS of 6.0×.

column2: What is the strategic objective of the My Items In-Grid ad placement?
column3: To drive retention and customer loyalty for consumables among logged-in repeat customers.

column2: What is the strategic objective of Stock Up ad placements on Walmart?
column3: To increase overall basket size and prompt replenishment purchases during the final stages of cart finalization.

column2: What is the minimum bid requirement for an Automatic Sponsored Products campaign on Walmart Connect?
column3: The minimum bid for an automatic campaign is $0.20.

column2: What is the minimum bid requirement for a Manual Sponsored Products campaign on Walmart Connect?
column3: The minimum bid for a manual campaign is $0.30.

column2: What is the minimum daily budget required for Walmart Sponsored Products campaigns?
column3: The minimum daily budget for both automatic and manual campaigns is $100.

column2: What is the minimum monthly spend requirement for Walmart Sponsored Products campaigns?
column3: The minimum monthly spend requirement for both automatic and manual campaigns is $1,000.

column2: What is the recommended overall minimum campaign budget per month for meaningful results on Walmart Connect?
column3: The recommended minimum budget is $4,500 per campaign per month.

column2: What organic search rank threshold must a product meet to be eligible for Sponsored Products ads?
column3: The product must rank organically within the top 128 search results for the targeted search term.

column2: What Listing Quality Score (LQS) threshold is recommended for optimal ad performance on Walmart?
column3: A Listing Quality Score above 80% is recommended.

column2: According to Walmart's Polaris algorithm, what percentage weight is assigned to Item Completeness?
column3: Item Completeness accounts for 40% of the algorithm's weighting.
